title: Comparison
description: The verdict of one run against a baseline. `inconclusive` is a first-class outcome: with stochastic decoding a single run pair cannot distinguish improvement from noise, and rounding toward a decision manufactures exactly the false confidence this subsystem exists to prevent.

refusal_reason.description: Required when verdict is `refused`. The comparator refuses rather than reporting a number when the two runs are not comparable: differing attribution tuples, unequalized detectors, or a suite whose declared resolution cannot see a delta this small.

test.description: Named per suite type and recorded, not improvised per comparison. Paired binary outcomes and graded or free-form metrics need different tests, and the choice is part of the result.

detectors_equalized.description: Whether both runs' detectors were shown to have comparable recall on the same ground truth. An intervention once appeared to raise hallucination by 10-15 points purely because structured output made failures easier to find; the effect reversed under a recall-equalized detector. Comparing unequalized detectors measures the instrument.
